column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|06-21|1914|Μπέρτα φον Ζούτνερ|Bertha von Suttner|Bertha von Suttner died in 1914, a few weeks before the outbreak of the First World War. She was an Austrian writer and pacifist, known for the book "Lay Down Your Arms!", and in 1905 she became the first woman to be awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|06-21|1953|Μπεναζίρ Μπούτο|Benazir Bhutto|Benazir Bhutto was a Pakistani politician and the daughter of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. In 1988 she became the first woman prime minister of a country with a Muslim majority. She was assassinated in 2007 at an election rally.

bio|06-21|1961|Τζόκο Ουιντόντο|Joko Widodo|Joko Widodo, known as Jokowi, is an Indonesian politician. He was mayor of Surakarta and governor of Jakarta, and from 2014 to 2024 he was president of Indonesia.

bio|06-21|1970|Σουκάρνο|Sukarno|Sukarno died in 1970. He was the first president of Indonesia, from 1945 to 1967, and he led the struggle for independence from the Netherlands. He was overthrown by Suharto.

bio|06-21|1979|Κρις Πρατ|Chris Pratt|Chris Pratt is an American actor. He became known through the series "Parks and Recreation", as Star-Lord in "Guardians of the Galaxy" and as Owen in "Jurassic World".

bio|06-21|1985|Λάνα Ντελ Ρέι|Lana Del Rey|Lana Del Rey is an American singer and songwriter. She is known for her melancholic and cinematic music, with songs such as "Video Games" and "Summertime Sadness".

bio|06-22|1727|Γεώργιος Α΄|George I|George I was king of Great Britain from 1714, the first of the House of Hanover. He was born in Germany and spoke little English, with the result that the power of his ministers increased. He died in Germany in 1727.

bio|06-22|1767|Βίλχελμ φον Χούμπολτ|Wilhelm von Humboldt|Wilhelm von Humboldt was a German philosopher, linguist and politician. He reformed education in Prussia and founded the University of Berlin. He was the brother of Alexander von Humboldt.

bio|06-22|1898|Έριχ Μαρία Ρεμάρκ|Erich Maria Remarque|Erich Maria Remarque was a German writer. He wrote the anti-war novel "All Quiet on the Western Front" about the First World War. The Nazis burned his books, and he emigrated to the United States.

bio|06-22|1906|Μπίλι Γουάιλντερ|Billy Wilder|Billy Wilder was born in what is now Poland and emigrated to the United States. He was a director and screenwriter, and he directed "Some Like It Hot" and "The Apartment". He won six Oscars.

bio|06-22|1949|Μέριλ Στριπ|Meryl Streep|Meryl Streep is an American actress. She is regarded as one of the finest actresses of her generation and has won three Oscars, for "Kramer vs. Kramer", "Sophie's Choice" and "The Iron Lady".

bio|06-22|1964|Νταν Μπράουν|Dan Brown|Dan Brown is an American writer. In 2003 he wrote the novel "The Da Vinci Code", which became one of the most successful books in the world, and other books starring the professor Robert Langdon.

bio|06-22|1969|Τζούντι Γκάρλαντ|Judy Garland|Judy Garland died in London in 1969, at the age of 47. She was an American actress and singer, known as Dorothy in "The Wizard of Oz", where she sang "Over the Rainbow".

bio|06-22|1987|Φρεντ Ασταίρ|Fred Astaire|Fred Astaire died in 1987. He was an American dancer and actor and one of the greatest dancers in film, with films such as "Top Hat", in which he danced with Ginger Rogers.
bio|06-22|1990|Ιλιά Φρανκ|Ilya Frank|Ilya Frank was a Soviet physicist. Together with Cherenkov and Tamm he explained the Cherenkov effect, and in 1958 they shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|06-23|79|Βεσπασιανός|Vespasian|Vespasian was Roman emperor from 69 to 79. He came to the throne after the civil war of the "Year of the Four Emperors" and founded the Flavian dynasty. He began the construction of the Colosseum.

bio|06-23|1889|Άννα Αχμάτοβα|Anna Akhmatova|Anna Akhmatova was a Russian poet and one of the most important poets of the 20th century. Her poem "Requiem" describes the suffering of the Stalin era. Despite persecution she continued to write.

bio|06-23|1891|Βίλχελμ Βέμπερ|Wilhelm Weber|Wilhelm Weber was a German physicist. He worked with Gauss on the study of magnetism, and they built one of the first electric telegraphs. The unit of magnetic flux, the weber, is named after him.

bio|06-23|1894|Εδουάρδος Η΄|Edward VIII|Edward VIII became king of the United Kingdom in 1936 and abdicated after a few months in order to marry the American Wallis Simpson. He became Duke of Windsor and lived in France.

bio|06-23|1912|Άλαν Τούρινγκ|Alan Turing|Alan Turing was born in London. He was a mathematician and a pioneer of computer science. He formulated the concept of the Turing machine and helped to break the Enigma code in the Second World War.

bio|06-23|1937|Μάρτι Αχτισάαρι|Martti Ahtisaari|Martti Ahtisaari is a Finnish diplomat and politician. He was president of Finland from 1994 to 2000 and mediated in conflicts in the Balkans and in Indonesia. In 2008 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|06-23|1959|Μπορίς Βιάν|Boris Vian|Boris Vian was a French writer, poet and jazz trumpeter. He wrote the novels "Froth on the Daydream" and "I Will Spit on Your Graves". He died young, at the age of 39.

bio|06-23|1972|Ζινεντίν Ζιντάν|Zinedine Zidane|Zinedine Zidane is a former French footballer of Algerian origin. He played as a midfielder for Juventus and Real Madrid, won the World Cup in 1998 and the European Championship in 2000. He later became a coach.
bio|06-23|1995|Τζόνας Σολκ|Jonas Salk|Jonas Salk was an American doctor and virologist. In 1955 he developed the first effective vaccine against polio, and he did not patent it.

bio|06-24|1519|Λουκρητία Βοργία|Lucrezia Borgia|Lucrezia Borgia died in 1519 in Ferrara. She was the daughter of Pope Alexander VI, and her marriages served the political alliances of the family. As Duchess of Ferrara she was a patron of the arts.

bio|06-24|1883|Βίκτορ Φραντς Ες|Victor Franz Hess|Victor Franz Hess was an Austrian physicist. In 1912, on balloon flights, he discovered cosmic radiation. In 1936 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Carl Anderson.

bio|06-24|1908|Γκρόβερ Κλίβελαντ|Grover Cleveland|Grover Cleveland died in 1908. He was the 22nd and the 24th president of the United States, and the only one to have served two non-consecutive terms, from 1885 to 1889 and from 1893 to 1897.
bio|06-24|1911|Χουάν Μανουέλ Φάντζιο|Juan Manuel Fangio|Juan Manuel Fangio was an Argentine racing driver. He won five Formula One world championships in the 1950s, a record that he held until 2003.

bio|06-24|1911|Ερνέστο Σάμπατο|Ernesto Sabato|Ernesto Sabato was an Argentine writer and physicist. He wrote the novels "The Tunnel" and "On Heroes and Tombs". He headed the commission that documented the crimes of the junta in Argentina.

bio|06-24|1915|Φρεντ Χόυλ|Fred Hoyle|Fred Hoyle was an English astronomer and writer. He studied the nuclear synthesis of stars and supported the "steady state" theory of the universe. He introduced the term "Big Bang", originally in a mocking tone.

bio|06-24|1935|Κάρλος Γαρδέλ|Carlos Gardel|Carlos Gardel was the greatest singer of Argentine tango. He became known around the world with songs such as "Por una cabeza" and "El día que me quieras". He was killed in an air crash in Colombia in 1935.

bio|06-24|1987|Λιονέλ Μέσι|Lionel Messi|Lionel Messi was born in Rosario, Argentina, and is a footballer. He played for Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Inter Miami, and he won the Ballon d'Or eight times. With Argentina he won the 2022 World Cup.
bio|06-24|2014|Ίλαϊ Γουάλακ|Eli Wallach|Eli Wallach was an American actor. He became known for the role of Tuco in "The Good, the Bad and the Ugly", and he appeared in "The Magnificent Seven".

bio|06-25|1852|Αντόνι Γκαουντί|Antoni Gaudí|Antoni Gaudí was a Catalan architect. He became known for his distinctive organic style, with works such as the Sagrada Família and Park Güell in Barcelona. He died in 1926.
bio|06-25|1856|Μαξ Στίρνερ|Max Stirner|Max Stirner was a German philosopher. His work "The Ego and Its Own" argues for individualism and is regarded as a forerunner of anarchism and existentialism.

bio|06-25|1864|Βάλτερ Νερνστ|Walther Nernst|Walther Nernst was a German chemist and physicist. He formulated the heat theorem, the third law of thermodynamics, and in 1920 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

bio|06-25|1903|Τζορτζ Όργουελ|George Orwell|George Orwell, real name Eric Blair, was born in India and was a British writer. He wrote "Animal Farm" and "1984", two works about totalitarianism. He died in 1950.

bio|06-25|1928|Αλεξέι Αλεξέγιεβιτς Αμπρικόσοφ|Alexei Abrikosov|Alexei Abrikosov was a Russian theoretical physicist. He studied superconductivity, and in 2003 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Ginzburg and Leggett.

bio|06-25|1963|Τζορτζ Μάικλ|George Michael|George Michael was an English singer. He started with the duo Wham! and continued as a solo artist with hits such as "Faith" and "Careless Whisper". He was also an activist for charitable causes. He died in 2016.

bio|06-25|1984|Μισέλ Φουκώ|Michel Foucault|Michel Foucault was a French philosopher and historian of ideas. He wrote "Discipline and Punish" and "The History of Sexuality", and he studied the relationship between power and knowledge. He died in 1984 from complications of AIDS.

bio|06-25|1997|Ζακ-Ιβ Κουστώ|Jacques-Yves Cousteau|Jacques-Yves Cousteau died in 1997. He was a French oceanographer and explorer who contributed to the development of underwater diving with breathing apparatus and made documentaries with the ship "Calypso".

bio|06-25|2009|Μάικλ Τζάκσον|Michael Jackson|Michael Jackson was an American singer and dancer, known as the "King of Pop". The album "Thriller" of 1982 is among the best-selling albums of all time. He died in Los Angeles in 2009.

bio|06-26|363|Ιουλιανός|Julian|Julian was Roman emperor from 361 to 363 and was called "the Apostate", because he tried to restore pagan worship. He was killed in 363 on a campaign against the Persians.

bio|06-26|1541|Φρανθίσκο Πιθάρρο|Francisco Pizarro|Francisco Pizarro was a Spanish conquistador. In 1532 he conquered the Inca Empire in Peru, capturing Atahualpa. He founded Lima in 1535 and was assassinated in 1541 by his rivals.

bio|06-26|1824|Ουίλιαμ Τόμσον|William Thomson, Lord Kelvin|William Thomson, Lord Kelvin, was an Irish physicist and engineer. He contributed to thermodynamics and proposed the absolute temperature scale, the Kelvin scale. He also worked on laying the first submarine telegraph cable across the Atlantic.

bio|06-26|1830|Γεώργιος Δ΄|George IV|George IV was king of the United Kingdom from 1820 to 1830. Before that he had been regent, and he was a patron of the arts. He was king when the Greek War of Independence began.
bio|06-26|1892|Περλ Μπακ|Pearl Buck|Pearl Buck was an American writer who grew up in China. She wrote the novel "The Good Earth" and in 1938 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-26|1908|Σαλβαδόρ Αλιέντε|Salvador Allende|Salvador Allende was a Chilean doctor and politician. In 1970 he became the first Marxist to be elected president of Chile in free elections. He was overthrown in 1973 by Pinochet's coup and died in the presidential palace.

bio|06-26|1943|Καρλ Λαντστάινερ|Karl Landsteiner|Karl Landsteiner was an Austrian biologist and doctor. He discovered the ABO blood groups, and in 1930 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

bio|06-26|1968|Πάολο Μαλντίνι|Paolo Maldini|Paolo Maldini is a former Italian footballer. He spent his entire career at Milan as a defender and won the Champions League five times. He was the son of Cesare Maldini.

bio|06-26|1993|Αριάνα Γκράντε|Ariana Grande|Ariana Grande is an American singer and actress. She became known through the series "Victorious" and with hits such as "Thank U, Next" and "7 Rings". She also appeared in the film "Wicked".

bio|06-27|1462|Λουδοβίκος ΙΒ΄|Louis XII|Louis XII was king of France from 1498 to 1515. He took part in the Italian Wars and conquered Milan. He was popular, and he was called the "Father of the People".

bio|06-27|1574|Τζόρτζο Βαζάρι|Giorgio Vasari|Giorgio Vasari was an Italian painter and architect from Arezzo. He wrote "Lives of the Most Excellent Painters, Sculptors, and Architects", an early history of Renaissance art. He also designed the building of the Uffizi.

bio|06-27|1844|Τζόζεφ Σμιθ|Joseph Smith|Joseph Smith was an American religious leader and the founder of the Latter Day Saint movement. He published the "Book of Mormon" in 1830. He was killed by a mob in 1844 in Illinois.

bio|06-27|1869|Έμμα Γκόλντμαν|Emma Goldman|Emma Goldman was born in Lithuania and emigrated to the United States. She was an anarchist and feminist, known for her speeches on freedom and birth control. She was deported to Russia in 1919.

bio|06-27|1880|Χέλεν Κέλερ|Helen Keller|Helen Keller was an American writer and activist. She became blind and deaf in infancy, but with the help of her teacher Annie Sullivan she learned to communicate and graduated from university.

bio|06-27|1975|Τόμπι Μαγκουάιρ|Tobey Maguire|Tobey Maguire is an American actor. He became known as Spider-Man in the trilogy of Sam Raimi. He also appeared in "The Cider House Rules" and "Seabiscuit".

bio|06-27|1977|Ραούλ Γκονθάλεθ|Raúl González|Raúl González is a former Spanish footballer. He played as a striker for Real Madrid for many years and is among the club's top scorers. He later became a coach.

bio|06-27|2001|Τόβε Γιάνσον|Tove Jansson|Tove Jansson was a Finnish writer and illustrator. She created the "Moomins", a series of books and comics for children with their characteristic little creatures.

bio|06-27|2001|Τζακ Λέμον|Jack Lemmon|Jack Lemmon was an American actor. He won the Academy Award for Best Actor for "Save the Tiger", and he appeared in "Some Like It Hot" and in "The Apartment" by Billy Wilder.
bio|06-28|1389|Μουράτ Α΄|Murad I|Murad I was Ottoman sultan from 1362 to 1389. He captured Adrianople and a large part of the Balkans. He was killed in 1389 at the Battle of Kosovo.

bio|06-28|1577|Πέτερ Πάουλ Ρούμπενς|Peter Paul Rubens|Peter Paul Rubens was a Flemish Baroque painter. He painted large works with mythological and religious themes, with dynamic movement, and he was also a diplomat. He had a large workshop in Antwerp.

bio|06-28|1712|Ζαν-Ζακ Ρουσσώ|Jean-Jacques Rousseau|Jean-Jacques Rousseau was born in Geneva. He was a philosopher of the Enlightenment. He wrote "The Social Contract" and "Émile" and argued that humans are naturally good and that society corrupts them.

bio|06-28|1836|Τζέιμς Μάντισον|James Madison|James Madison died in 1836. He was the 4th president of the United States and is regarded as the "father of the Constitution". With others he wrote "The Federalist Papers".

bio|06-28|1867|Λουίτζι Πιραντέλλο|Luigi Pirandello|Luigi Pirandello was an Italian writer and playwright. He wrote "Six Characters in Search of an Author" and "Henry IV". In 1934 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-28|1914|Φραγκίσκος Φερδινάνδος|Franz Ferdinand|Franz Ferdinand was an Archduke of Austria and heir to the throne. He was assassinated on 28 June 1914 in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip, an event that led to the First World War.

bio|06-28|1940|Μοχάμεντ Γιουνούς|Muhammad Yunus|Muhammad Yunus is an economist from Bangladesh. He founded the Grameen Bank, which gives small loans to the poor. In 2006 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize together with the bank.

bio|06-28|1971|Ίλον Μασκ|Elon Musk|Elon Musk was born in South Africa. He is a businessman and head of the companies Tesla and SpaceX, and owner of the platform X, formerly Twitter. He co-founded PayPal.

bio|06-28|1992|Μιχαήλ Ταλ|Mikhail Tal|Mikhail Tal was a Latvian chess player. In 1960 he became world champion at the age of 23. He was known for his aggressive and spectacular style of play, which earned him the nickname "the Magician from Riga".

bio|06-29|1326|Μουράτ Α΄|Murad I|Murad I was Ottoman sultan who reigned from 1362 to 1389. He captured Adrianople, which became the capital, and a large part of the Balkans. He was killed at the Battle of Kosovo.

bio|06-29|1798|Τζάκομο Λεοπάρντι|Giacomo Leopardi|Giacomo Leopardi was an Italian poet from Recanati. He wrote the "Canti", with poems such as "The Infinite", and many philosophical works in a pessimistic tone. He died young, in 1837.

bio|06-29|1861|Ελίζαμπεθ Μπάρετ Μπράουνινγκ|Elizabeth Barrett Browning|Elizabeth Barrett Browning died in 1861 in Florence. She was an English poet and wrote the "Sonnets from the Portuguese", love poems for her husband Robert Browning.

bio|06-29|1895|Τόμας Χάξλεϋ|Thomas Huxley|Thomas Huxley died in 1895. He was an English biologist who defended Darwin's theory of evolution and earned the nickname "Darwin's bulldog". He introduced the term "agnosticism".

bio|06-29|1900|Αντουάν ντε Σαιντ-Εξυπερύ|Antoine de Saint-Exupéry|Antoine de Saint-Exupéry was a French writer and pilot. He wrote "The Little Prince" in 1943, one of the best-known books in the world. He disappeared in 1944 on a reconnaissance flight over the Mediterranean.

bio|06-29|1925|Τζόρτζιο Ναπολιτάνο|Giorgio Napolitano|Giorgio Napolitano was an Italian politician. He was president of Italy from 2006 to 2015 and the only president to have been re-elected for a second term, in 2013.
bio|06-29|1940|Πάουλ Κλέε|Paul Klee|Paul Klee was a Swiss painter. He taught at the Bauhaus and made works with a poetic and playful style, with many colours and shapes. He died in 1940.

bio|06-29|1957|Κουρμπανγκουλί Μπερντιμουχαμέντοφ|Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow|Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow is a Turkmen politician. He was president of Turkmenistan from 2007 to 2022, when he handed power to his son. He also holds the title of "Arkadag".
bio|06-29|2003|Κάθριν Χέπμπορν|Katharine Hepburn|Katharine Hepburn died in 2003. She was an American actress who won four Academy Awards for Best Actress, a record that still stands.
bio|06-30|1470|Κάρολος Η΄|Charles VIII|Charles VIII was king of France from 1483 to 1498. In 1494 he invaded Italy and began the Italian Wars. He died suddenly in 1498.

bio|06-30|1911|Τσέσλαφ Μίλος|Czesław Miłosz|Czesław Miłosz was a Polish poet and writer. He left communist Poland and lived in the United States. He wrote "The Captive Mind", and in 1980 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-30|1919|Τζον Ουίλιαμ Στρατ|John William Strutt|John William Strutt, Lord Rayleigh, was an English physicist. He studied the scattering of light and discovered argon together with Ramsay. In 1904 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|06-30|1934|Κουρτ φον Σλάιχερ|Kurt von Schleicher|Kurt von Schleicher was a German general and chancellor in 1932 and 1933, before Hitler. He was murdered by the Nazis during the Night of the Long Knives, together with his wife.

bio|06-30|1954|Σερζ Σαρκισιάν|Serzh Sargsyan|Serzh Sargsyan is an Armenian politician. He was president of Armenia from 2008 to 2018 and then prime minister for a few days in 2018, before resigning because of protests.
bio|06-30|1961|Λη ντε Φόρεστ|Lee de Forest|Lee de Forest was an American inventor. He invented the triode vacuum tube (Audion) in 1906, which helped in the development of radio and electronics.
bio|06-30|1966|Μάικ Τάισον|Mike Tyson|Mike Tyson is an American former boxer. In 1986, at the age of 20, he became the youngest heavyweight world champion. He was known for his power and aggression.

bio|06-30|1985|Μάικλ Φελπς|Michael Phelps|Michael Phelps is an American swimmer. He has won more Olympic medals than anyone in history, 28 in all, 23 of them gold, and in 2008 he won eight gold medals at a single Olympic Games.

bio|06-30|2017|Σιμόν Βέιλ|Simone Veil|Simone Veil was a French politician and an Auschwitz survivor. As minister of health she secured the legalisation of abortion in France in 1975, and from 1979 she was the first president of the European Parliament.

bio|07-01|1646|Γκότφριντ Βίλχελμ Λάιμπνιτς|Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz|Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was a German philosopher and mathematician. He developed calculus independently of Newton and introduced the notation that is used today. He argued that we live in "the best of all possible worlds".

bio|07-01|1804|Γεωργία Σάνδη|George Sand|George Sand, real name Amantine Aurore Lucile Dupin, was a French writer. She wrote novels such as "Little Fadette" and was known for her independent life, with relationships with Chopin and Musset.
bio|07-01|1876|Μιχαήλ Μπακούνιν|Mikhail Bakunin|Mikhail Bakunin died in 1876 in Bern. He was a Russian revolutionary and theorist of anarchism, and he clashed with Marx in the First International.

bio|07-01|1896|Χάριετ Μπίτσερ Στόου|Harriet Beecher Stowe|Harriet Beecher Stowe died in 1896. She was an American writer who wrote the anti-slavery novel "Uncle Tom's Cabin", which had great influence before the Civil War.

bio|07-01|1961|Νταϊάνα|Diana, Princess of Wales|Diana Spencer was born in England and in 1981 married Prince Charles, becoming Princess of Wales. She was known for her charitable work. She was killed in a road accident in Paris in 1997.

bio|07-01|1961|Λουί-Φερντινάν Σελίν|Louis-Ferdinand Céline|Louis-Ferdinand Céline was a French writer and doctor. He wrote the novel "Journey to the End of the Night", a work with a modernist style and spoken language. He was controversial because of his antisemitic writings.
bio|07-01|1967|Πάμελα Άντερσον|Pamela Anderson|Pamela Anderson is a Canadian actress and model. She became known through the series "Baywatch" and as a Playboy model.
bio|07-01|1986|Agnez Mo|Agnez Mo|Agnez Mo is an Indonesian singer, songwriter and actress. She became known in Indonesia as a child and later developed an international career.
bio|07-01|2004|Μάρλον Μπράντο|Marlon Brando|Marlon Brando died in 2004. He was an American actor who won Oscars for "On the Waterfront" and "The Godfather". He deeply influenced acting.

bio|07-02|1778|Ζαν Ζακ Ρουσσώ|Jean-Jacques Rousseau|Jean-Jacques Rousseau died in 1778 at Ermenonville. He was a Swiss philosopher of the Enlightenment and wrote "The Social Contract", "Émile" and "The Confessions".

bio|07-02|1862|Ουίλιαμ Χένρι Μπραγκ|William Henry Bragg|William Henry Bragg was an English physicist. Together with his son Lawrence he developed X-ray crystallography, and in 1915 they shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|07-02|1877|Χέρμαν Έσσε|Hermann Hesse|Hermann Hesse was a German-Swiss writer. He wrote the novels "Steppenwolf", "Siddhartha" and "The Glass Bead Game". In 1946 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|07-02|1923|Βισλάβα Συμπόρσκα|Wisława Szymborska|Wisława Szymborska was a Polish poet. Her poetry has irony and a philosophical outlook. In 1996 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She died in 2012.

bio|07-02|1925|Πατρίς Λουμούμπα|Patrice Lumumba|Patrice Lumumba was the first prime minister of independent Congo, in 1960. He was deposed, arrested and killed in 1961, in a crisis involving foreign interventions. He became a symbol of Africa's struggle for independence.

bio|07-02|1929|Ιμέλντα Μάρκος|Imelda Marcos|Imelda Marcos is a Filipino politician and the wife of the dictator Ferdinand Marcos. She became known for her luxury, including her collection of shoes. After the fall of the regime in 1986 she returned to the country and to politics.

bio|07-02|1937|Αμέλια Έρχαρτ|Amelia Earhart|Amelia Earhart was an American aviator. In 1932 she became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic by aeroplane. She disappeared in 1937 during an attempt to fly around the world.

bio|07-02|1961|Έρνεστ Χέμινγουεϊ|Ernest Hemingway|Ernest Hemingway was an American writer. He wrote "The Old Man and the Sea", "For Whom the Bell Tolls" and "A Farewell to Arms". In 1954 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He took his own life in 1961.
bio|07-02|1977|Βλαντίμιρ Ναμπόκοφ|Vladimir Nabokov|Vladimir Nabokov died in 1977 in Switzerland. He was a Russian writer who wrote in Russian and in English, and he is known for "Lolita".

bio|07-03|1423|Λουδοβίκος ΙΑ΄|Louis XI|Louis XI was king of France from 1461 to 1483. He strengthened royal power and limited the power of the nobles. He was called the "Universal Spider" because of his political intrigues.

bio|07-03|1642|Μαρία των Μεδίκων|Marie de' Medici|Marie de' Medici was queen of France as the wife of Henry IV and regent for her son Louis XIII. She fell into disgrace, was exiled, and died in Cologne in 1642.

bio|07-03|1883|Φραντς Κάφκα|Franz Kafka|Franz Kafka was born in Prague. He was a Czech Jewish writer who wrote in German. He wrote "The Metamorphosis", "The Trial" and "The Castle". He died in 1924, and most of his works were published after his death.

bio|07-03|1904|Τέοντορ Χερτσλ|Theodor Herzl|Theodor Herzl was an Austro-Hungarian journalist and the founder of political Zionism. His book "The Jewish State" and the first Zionist Congress in 1897 led to the creation of the movement. He died in 1904.

bio|07-03|1918|Μωάμεθ Ε΄|Mehmed V|Mehmed V was Ottoman sultan from 1909 to 1918. During his reign the Balkan Wars and the First World War took place, with the Ottoman Empire on the side of the Central Powers. He died in 1918.
